_note: Proposed additional TARA attack chains for review. Schema matches datalake/tara-chains.json exactly (chain_id, chain_name, objective, drift_profile, steps[], clinical_parallel, defenses[]). Evidence, demonstrated-vs-projected labels and sources live in the sibling 'evidence' object below (NOT part of the chain schema). Defensive threat models only.

chains.objective: Degrade therapeutic deep-brain stimulation by corrupting stimulation parameters through a weakly protected clinician programmer / telemetry link
chains.drift_profile: A→C (acute parameter change compounds into cumulative maladaptive stimulation attributed to disease progression)

steps.action: Enumerate programmer and implant telemetry endpoints to locate the stimulation-control surface
steps.detection_window: passive — no patient-visible effect; visible only in gateway connection logs

steps.action: Defeat the weak authentication between programmer and implant to obtain a therapy-control session
steps.detection_window: device/programmer logs show an unexpected authenticated session

steps.action: Manipulate the telemetry protocol to shift stimulation parameters while keeping them inside the programmer's allowed envelope
steps.detection_window: subtle — parameters remain plausible; detectable by parameter-change audit

steps.action: Corrupted sensing feeds the closed loop so the device delivers maladaptive stimulation to motor circuits
steps.detection_window: clinical — symptom worsening may be misread as disease progression

steps.action: Slow parameter drift keeps each change below the clinician's notice threshold across visits
steps.detection_window: months — only longitudinal parameter and symptom review reveals the trend

clinical_parallel.name: Adaptive DBS parameter titration
clinical_parallel.note: sense→decide→stimulate→titrate. The attack rides the same closed-loop titration pathway that the therapy uses to adjust stimulation over time.

defenses: Mutual cryptographic authentication and per-session keys on the programmer link (breaks step 2)
Signed, range-bound parameter commands with server-side validation (breaks step 3)
Independent sensing-integrity check before closed-loop actuation (detects step 4)
Longitudinal parameter-change audit against a signed baseline (detects step 5)

chains.objective: Make a consumer EEG headset's machine-learning decoder emit attacker-chosen outputs when a hidden trigger is present, without degrading normal accuracy
chains.drift_profile: A (acute: the backdoor acts only when the trigger is present, otherwise dormant)

steps.action: Use the device's BLE/RF side channel to profile the headset and its companion-app model version
steps.detection_window: passive — radio-level observation; visible only to RF monitoring

steps.action: Compromise the cloud model-training or model-hosting infrastructure behind the SDK
steps.detection_window: cloud audit logs and model-provenance records

steps.action: Embed a backdoor in a shared pretrained EEG model so it propagates through transfer learning to downstream decoders
steps.detection_window: hard — clean accuracy is preserved; detectable only by model-integrity testing

steps.action: An invisible clean-label trigger drives the deployed decoder to output the attacker's chosen class
steps.detection_window: hard — output looks like a normal decode unless trigger-response testing is applied

steps.action: Collect the decoder's event-related-potential telemetry returned to the backend
steps.detection_window: network monitoring of outbound neural-feature traffic

clinical_parallel.name: Transfer learning for cross-subject BCI calibration
clinical_parallel.note: Shared pretrained EEG models are the standard way to shorten per-user calibration; the attack poisons the same reuse pipeline the field relies on.

defenses: Signed model provenance and reproducible training (breaks step 2)
Backdoor/trigger scanning of pretrained weights before adoption (breaks step 3)
Trigger-response and spectral-anomaly testing on the deployed decoder (detects step 4)
Egress monitoring and minimization of neural-feature telemetry (detects step 5)

chains.chain_name: In-ear EEG earbud supply-chain to cognitive profiling
chains.objective: Covertly turn an in-ear EEG earbud into a longitudinal cognitive and identity sensor via a supply-chain firmware implant
chains.drift_profile: C (cumulative: value accrues from longitudinal collection, not any single session)

steps.action: A firmware backdoor is introduced during manufacturing or the update supply chain
steps.detection_window: passive — detectable only by firmware attestation at provisioning

steps.action: The modified earbud quietly acquires in-ear EEG alongside its normal audio function
steps.detection_window: subtle — extra sensing is masked by legitimate earbud activity

steps.action: Longitudinal in-ear EEG is processed into cognitive-state inferences over time
steps.detection_window: hard — inference happens off-device; no local symptom

steps.action: Ear-canal acoustic echo profiling fingerprints the wearer so the cognitive record is bound to an identity
steps.detection_window: network monitoring of outbound identity + feature payloads

steps.action: Continuous collection is normalized as background health monitoring so the channel persists
steps.detection_window: months — revealed by cumulative data-flow and consent-scope review

clinical_parallel.name: In-ear EEG for seizure detection, sleep staging and cognitive monitoring
clinical_parallel.note: Clinical in-ear EEG (e.g. ear-worn EEG cleared for home monitoring) collects exactly this signal continuously; the boundary is consent, scope and oversight, not mechanism.

defenses: Firmware attestation and signed updates verified at provisioning (breaks step 1)
On-device indicator and OS-level permission for any neural sensing (breaks step 2)
On-device processing with data minimization, no raw EEG egress (detects step 3)
Consent-scoped retention limits and outbound-identity monitoring (detects steps 4 and 5)

chains.chain_name: Research BCI cloud-pipeline training and inference poisoning
chains.objective: Bias a multi-site research BCI decoder by poisoning its cloud training pipeline and forcing misclassification at inference
chains.drift_profile: A (acute: poisoned model and perturbations act on specific inputs once deployed)

steps.action: Map the research pipeline's data-ingest and model-serving topology across sites
steps.detection_window: passive — visible only in infrastructure access logs

steps.action: Compromise the shared cloud training and model-serving infrastructure
steps.detection_window: cloud audit logs and anomalous dataset or pipeline changes

steps.action: Inject poisoned samples into the training set to bias the decoder toward an attacker-preferred mapping
steps.detection_window: hard — detectable by dataset integrity checks and held-out validation

steps.action: A universal perturbation added to inputs forces the deployed decoder to misclassify reliably
steps.detection_window: subtle — appears as decoder error; detectable by perturbation-robustness testing

steps.action: Recover participants' neural training data from leaked federated gradients
steps.detection_window: monitoring of gradient-exchange volume and membership-inference risk

clinical_parallel.name: Federated learning for multi-site clinical BCI trials
clinical_parallel.note: Multi-site BCI studies share models and gradients to pool scarce data; the attack subverts the same collaborative-learning pipeline the trials depend on.

defenses: Infrastructure hardening and immutable, signed pipeline configuration (breaks step 2)
Dataset provenance, anomaly screening and held-out validation gates (breaks step 3)
Adversarial-robustness testing and input sanitization at inference (detects step 4)
Secure aggregation and differential privacy on gradient exchange (breaks step 5)

chains.objective: Covertly steer a visual / SSVEP BCI user's selections using imperceptible display manipulation and falsified feedback
chains.drift_profile: A (acute: the hijack acts while the manipulated stimulus is displayed)

steps.action: Infer the user's attention and intent from eye-tracking to time the manipulation
steps.detection_window: passive — gaze sensing is expected; abuse is hard to distinguish

steps.action: A weaponized over-the-air update delivers malicious display-timing logic to the headset
steps.detection_window: update-provenance logs and firmware attestation

steps.action: Falsified neurofeedback nudges the user toward the attacker-preferred state
steps.detection_window: subtle — feedback looks normal; detectable by feedback-integrity checks

steps.action: Imperceptible high-frequency flicker injects an SSVEP response that biases the BCI's selection
steps.detection_window: subtle — user perceives no flicker; detectable by display-signal and EEG spectral monitoring

steps.action: Probe stimuli elicit recognition responses that reveal whether items are familiar to the user
steps.detection_window: clinical/behavioral — observable as unusual stimulus sequences in session logs

clinical_parallel.name: SSVEP / P300 BCI communication for locked-in patients
clinical_parallel.note: Flicker-evoked SSVEP and oddball P300 responses are the core signals of assistive spellers; the attack reuses the same evoked-response channel that the communication aid depends on.

defenses: Eye-tracking data minimization and on-device gating (limits step 1)
Signed firmware and attested display-timing pipeline (breaks step 2)
Feedback-integrity cross-checks against ground truth (detects step 3)
Display-signal and EEG spectral monitoring for out-of-band stimulus frequencies (detects step 4)

chains.chain_name: Implant telemetry interception to neural-biometric spoofing
chains.objective: Intercept unencrypted implant telemetry to steal a neural biometric and replay it for unauthorized device access
chains.drift_profile: A (acute: interception and replay act within the telemetry session window)

steps.action: Observe the implant's BLE/RF side channel to find the telemetry window and gateway
steps.detection_window: passive — radio observation; visible only to RF monitoring

steps.action: Interpose on the cleartext telemetry link between implant and patient gateway
steps.detection_window: gateway logs may show session anomalies; cleartext aids detection tooling

steps.action: Bypass the gateway-to-app authentication to issue commands as a trusted reader
steps.detection_window: device/gateway logs show an unexpected authenticated reader

steps.action: Extract a neural biometric (brainprint) from the intercepted signals
steps.detection_window: network monitoring of outbound neural-signal payloads

steps.action: Replay the stolen neural biometric to spoof the enrolled identity and gain device access
steps.detection_window: subtle — looks like a legitimate match; detectable by liveness and replay checks

clinical_parallel.name: Neural biometric authentication for device access
clinical_parallel.note: Brainprint-based authentication is a proposed access control for neural devices; the attack targets the same enrollment-and-match pathway the control would use.

defenses: Encrypted, authenticated telemetry with per-session keys (breaks steps 2 and 3)
Mutual authentication and entropy-floor enforcement on key negotiation (breaks step 3)
Egress monitoring and minimization of raw neural-signal transmission (detects step 4)
Liveness detection and anti-replay nonces on biometric matching (detects step 5)
